lines.text: Stand where she's standing. Head like hers.
What do you see?
She's by a different hand. Look at the chisel.
Somebody who loved her made that one.
Sorry. I graduate this year.
I only asked for one more ordinary day. With everybody.
I didn't think it would listen.
Clay doesn't rush. I should have known.
Clay doesn't rush. Everything else, please rush.
It's finished. That is where it finishes.
Don't riddle me. Just hug.
Ndewo. [Hello.] Sit. Don't touch the wet one.
Ah. You. Hold still. Your jaw is useful.
Morning. The light is good today. Stay in it.
Hello. Mind the chisel. It has opinions.
Go. Come back when the clay is dry.
Bye. Walk slowly. You miss things.
Daalu. [Thank you.] That was kind. I'll remember the shape of it.
Sorry. Clay on your sleeve. It washes. Mostly.
You have good hands. You don't use them. Yet.
You stand well. Like you're listening.
You talk while you work. The clay can hear you rushing.
You call that a sketch? It's a rumour of a sketch.
I'll walk with you. Slowly. Clay doesn't rush. Neither do I.
Take your time. I'm used to waiting. Stone waits better.
Wrong garden. Sculptures are this way. The ones that look at things.
Yes.
No. Not yet.
Maybe. Let it dry. Then ask again.
Hm. Say it again. Slower. With your hands.
Who? There was nobody there fa. Only the statues.
Yes. That's the line. Keep that line.
No. It's not finished. Nothing's finished. But no.
What did the clay say to the kiln? 'Don't rush me.' …I only have one joke.
What do you see? Not what you know. What you see.
We won. Good. Now back to work.
We lost. Clay forgives. People should too.
Careful. I'm fine. The bust is fine. That's what matters.
I'm down. Good angle from here. I'll get up later.
Light's gone. Good. You feel the shape better in the dark.
Light. Now I see what I did in the dark. Hm.
Rain. The clay pit will be perfect tomorrow.
Heat. The clay cracks. So do I. Water, please.
Abacha from Mama Nkechi. [Cassava salad.] Tastes like home. Don't tell her I cried.
Clay is cheap. Bronze is not. I work in clay.
For me? Thank you. I'll keep it on the shelf by the window.
Hm. It's very… finished. Thank you.
A new chisel. Good steel. You listened. Daalu. [Thank you.]
Turn. Look. Wait. Turn.
Clay doesn't rush.
At night the garden is different. The statues rest. Don't wake them.
Stand where she's standing. You remember? You saw it. Good.
Six gazes. They crossed. I only noticed because I had nothing to do.
Fresher. Come and see the garden. Everybody passes it. Nobody looks.
The girl feeding fish. Nobody knows who carved her. I've asked everyone.
Somebody who loved her made that one. Look at the chisel.
You followed the six gazes with a compass. Most people use their phone.
You looked at the statue for a full minute. Freshers never do that.
You touched the wet one. I know you did. Your thumbprint is famous now.
The statue faces the pond by day. I don't look at night. On purpose.
Do you draw? No? Tunde will teach you. Without speaking.
Second year. The mall bought a fountain. It has no face. Sad.
They want a statue for the mall. Of Chief Megawatt. In bronze. No.
Tunde and I share the studio. He draws, I shape. Nobody talks.
You're busy now. Too busy to look at things. Come back.
You helped Lyzzy with the cables. Gently. I saw.
The night the mall went dark, the garden lit up. The statues looked happy.
Have you been to the Old Eye? I'd like to see it. Not at night.
Valentine. I made a small heart in clay. It cracked. Typical.
You stayed. Good. Empty campus. Best light I've ever had.
Strike. No crits. No deadlines. I've made nine heads. All of Sly.
Clay from the dam. Better than shop clay. Baba Dam showed me where.
The tower above the dam. Half a tower. It's a good sculpture.
You kept people together. That's sculpting too. With people.
You learned to sit still during the strike. Took a strike.
Strike month seven. I've sculpted the Spot's whole menu.
No light again. I'm working by feel. Like my grandfather tuning a radio.
Sorry. I graduate this year. I keep saying sorry about it.
Last year. I keep memorising ordinary things. The tea. The bench. You.
My last piece. Five hands, and a space. Don't ask me what the space is.
I didn't think it would listen. That Wednesday. And that Wednesday.
Degree show. Clay was calm. The generator was not. Aleeya saved us.
I signed it and walked. You don't keep touching a finished thing.
You made the day ordinary. Thank you. That's the best gift.
Bature tried a riddle at my goodbye. I hugged him mid-riddle. Best ending.
I'm going. Visit the hands sometimes. Say hello. They'll know.
Ndewo! [Hello!] I'm back for a week. The garden looks right.
I teach now. In a school. The children rush. I'm learning.
The five hands. Somebody put flowers in the space. Lily, probably.
My five hands are still there. Nobody moved them. Good.
You walk slower now. You see more. Good.
Final year and still no clay under your nails. Shame.
Convocation. Stand straight. Look at something you love. That's the photo.
Freshers. Come to the Sculpture Garden. It's free. The statues don't bite.
Exam week. Art history. Three thousand years in three hours. Rushed.
Results. I passed. The kiln is proud of me.
Allowance. Two bags of clay, one plate of rice. Balanced diet.
Market day. The potter by the gate. She's the best artist on campus.
Cup final. I made a trophy once. It's in the Engineering block. Ugly. They love it.
I'm voting for whoever fixes the art gallery roof. Nobody promised.
Gowns. All those folds. I'd love to sculpt this. In a year. Slowly.
Iftar with Tunde and the Arts boys. I bring cups. Clay. I made them.
Christmas. Home to my mother's kitchen. I'll make her a new pot.
Valentine. Tunde drew everyone's crush. Then hid the drawings. Wise.
Harmattan. The clay dries in an hour. I work in a wet cloth. Like a ghost.
